column1: # THE POPULATION P1's CONTRACT MUST COVER: every (channel, level) pair
# `BaselineConfiguredThresholds::resolve()` walks, with the options object that
# pair actually resolves to, and TWO INDEPENDENT WITNESSES of whether that
# object holds a configured warning boundary.
# Regenerate with:
#   php docs/internal/plans/rule-vocabulary/enumeration-configured-boundary-population.php
# (the generator is committed next to this file; it boots the real container,
# reflects the service out of BaselineExplainCommand and prints the rows below).
# ROW COUNT: 49 channel-level pairs over 39 distinct resolved options classes.
# THIS TABLE ENUMERATES PATHS, NOT CLASSES, and the difference is not empty.
# The companion `enumeration-boundary-contract-implementors.tsv` enumerates the
# classes a contract obligation would land on. Six of them never appear as a
# `resolved_options` value here — five hierarchical parents, whose levels are
# what the walk resolves to, and `ComputedMetricRuleOptions`, whose rule declares
# no channel statically. A conclusion about "every class that must implement the
# method" cannot be drawn from this file.
# THE TWO WITNESSES, and why one is not enough:
#   - `warning_named_members` — the public numeric members whose NAME says
#     "warning". This is the witness today's code uses, through a hardcoded list
#     of three names, and it is the one being removed.
#   - `severity_switch_points` — the values at which `getSeverity()` actually
#     changes its answer, found by probing a grid. Behaviour, not naming. A
#     `X` in this column marks a value where `getSeverity()` threw: an exception
#     is not an absent severity, and the generator refuses to conflate them.
#     THIS COLUMN IS A COARSE SWEEP, FOR READING. It is not the definition a
#     check may use: a grid says only "between these two probes". The normative
#     definition lives in the plan (`P1-configured-boundary.md`, "Одно
#     определение точки переключения") and probes the neighbourhood
#     {b-1, b, b+1} of one candidate, because an exclusive comparison with an
#     int cast puts the switch at b+1 and a grid can straddle it unseen.
#   A declaration that names the wrong member passes the first witness and fails
#   the second; a rule that judges without `getSeverity()` fails the second while
#   holding a perfectly real boundary. Only the disagreements are interesting,
#   and they are enumerated below rather than left to be discovered.
# THE DISAGREEMENTS, all five of them. THREE ARE MISSED BOUNDARIES, not the one
# this file first claimed — the correction is recorded here rather than quietly
# applied, because the wrong reading is what a reader of the earlier version
# acted on:
#   - `coupling.distance` — `maxDistanceWarning=0.3` is configured AND is where
#     `getSeverity()` switches, and the old reader printed nothing, because
#     `maxDistanceWarning` was not one of the three names it guessed at.
#   - `design.god-class` — switches at "> 0", which is NOT its boundary, and the
#     first reading stopped there and called the refusal correct. `GodClassRule`
#     reports `$matchedCount` and warns from `matchedCount >= minCriteria`
#     upwards, deciding inside `analyze()`; `minCriteria` is configurable, is
#     where `withOverride()` puts the warning half, and is a real boundary on
#     the axis the channel reports. `getSeverity()` is a stub and witnesses
#     nothing here.
#   - `design.data-class` — constant `Warning`, and again the first reading
#     called that "no boundary". `DataClassRule` reports WOC, declares
#     `WorseDirection::Lower`, and emits while `woc <= wocThreshold`.
#     `wmcThreshold` gates a second metric, exactly as `minAfferent`,
#     `minClassCount` and `minStatements` gate elsewhere without stopping their
#     classes from naming a boundary.
#   - `code-smell.long-parameter-list` — `getSeverity()` switches at 4, and the
#     object also holds `voWarning=8`, applied by `LongParameterListRule`
#     through a separate `getVoSeverity()` when the callable is a value object's
#     constructor. One channel, two boundaries, chosen by a property of the
#     subject. Printing nothing is the correct answer.
#   - `architecture.circular-dependency` — switches at 3, and no member is named
#     for it: severity comes from the cycle's length against the boolean
#     `directAsError`, not from a number `qmx.yaml` places on an axis. Printing
#     nothing is correct.
# WHY THE FIRST READING WENT WRONG, because the mechanism outlives the two rows.
# `getSeverity()` was treated as the authority on whether a boundary exists. It
# is the authority only for rules that delegate to it. A rule that decides in
# `analyze()` leaves behind a stub whose behaviour says "no boundary" no matter
# what the class holds — so for those, absence of a switch point is not evidence
# of absence of a boundary, and the emission condition inside the rule has to be
# read. `WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE` said this in the abstract and the
# analysis above it then resolved it the wrong way.
# The 17 rows with `(none)` under `warning_named_members` and a switch at 0.01
# are occurrence detectors: severity depends on the count of occurrences against
# a hardcoded "more than zero", not against anything `qmx.yaml` can move. They
# have no configured boundary, and that is a statement about them, not a gap.
# WHAT THE ROWS DO SUPPORT: every row whose `current_explain_output` is a number
# has `threshold_aware=yes`, and no row with `threshold_aware=no` holds a
# warning-named member at all (both counts are 0 by `awk` over this file). The
# holders of a configured boundary are therefore already inside
# `ThresholdAwareOptionsInterface` — which is the population the contract lands
# on, and it is 27 classes rather than every options class in the tree.
# THREE CLASSES SERVE MORE THAN ONE CHANNEL: `CodeSmellOptions` (7),
# `SecurityPatternOptions` (3) and `TypeCoverageOptions` (3). None of them
# serves two channels with two DIFFERENT boundaries: the first two hold no
# boundary at all, and the third is instantiated once per rule under its own
# rule name. That, and not "only TypeCoverageOptions repeats", is what licenses
# a contract method with no channel argument.
# `complexity.npath|class` resolves a boundary while its level is DISABLED.
# Configured and enabled are different columns; the current output keeps them
# apart, and so must the replacement.
# WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE
# - Values are the classes' DEFAULTS, not this repository's configuration. The
#   generator builds the container through `ContainerFactory` alone, which does
#   not read `qmx.yaml`: the file sets `max_distance_warning: 0.5` for
#   `coupling.distance` and this table shows 0.3. Which member is the boundary
#   does not depend on configuration; the numbers do, and these are not the
#   numbers a `bin/qmx check` in this repository would judge against.
# - The probe grid is discrete. A switch between two grid points is invisible;
#   `coupling.class-rank`'s 0.02 was missed by the first grid and only appeared
#   once the grid was extended, which is exactly how this blind spot fails.
# - Channels no rule declares statically. `ComputedMetricRule` declares none, so
#   `explain` resolves no computed-metric channel at all — a gap in
#   `ChannelDeclarationReader`'s reach, not in this table's.
# - `getSeverity()` witnesses only the rules that delegate to it: 25 `*Rule.php`
#   files call it (`grep -rln 'getSeverity(' src --include='*Rule.php'`), and the
#   three that hold or refuse a boundary without delegating are named above.
# - Test doubles implementing `RuleOptionsInterface` are not rules and are absent
#   here; they are counted in the implementors enumeration instead.
